notes: Tier: HTTP-first for robots.txt/sitemaps (no Claude-specific disallow found), then Playwright (site is an Angular/SAP Commerce Cloud SPA with no SSR HTML - direct HTTP fetch of category pages returns an empty app shell). Discovery: fetched categorysitemap.xml (938 URLs, all nav category PLPs) and grepped case-insensitively for christmas/xmas/halloween/diwali/easter/valentine/thanksgiving/new-year/festive/holiday/seasonal/festival/lunar/melbourne-cup/mothers-day/fathers-day - only '/c/christmas' matched (appears twice = duplicate sitemap entries, same page). Also rendered the full mega-nav (all top-level menus: SOFAS, DINING & KITCHENS, LIVING ROOM & OFFICE, BEDROOM, MATTRESSES, OUTDOOR, HOMEWARES, RUGS, WALL ART, LIFESTYLE, SALE) via Playwright on the Christmas page (site loads the complete mega-menu on every page) and re-ran the same keyword grep over all ~800 nav links + body text - no other holiday/seasonal category found anywhere in the site taxonomy. Confirmed via the site's own category API (api-prod.freedom.com.au/greenlitrest/v2/freedomfurniture/searchCategory?categoryCode=christmas) which returns the canonical Christmas category tree with exactly 4 genuine sub-categories (christmas-trees, christmas-decor, christmas-foliage, christmas-dining-and-kitchen) - confirming completeness of the discovered set. Excluded: 'SHOP GIFTING' (/c/all-gifts) is a generic sitewide gift-finder, not Christmas-specific; 'SHOP E-GIFT CARDS' links off-site to giftcard.freedom.com.au and is not a product PLP - both excluded as not genuinely Christmas-scoped categories. The /c/christmas landing page itself displays '148 PRODUCTS' but is a rollup/landing view built from the same 4 sub-categories (whose PLP-displayed counts are 111+15+17+18=161, differing from 148 due to normal facet/product overlap across sub-categories on this platform) - per the grouping rule this parent is kept as a name-only grouping row (is_group true, qty/link null) and the 4 sub-categories are the counted rows, avoiding double-counting. Each sub-category qty is the exact 'N PRODUCTS' count shown on its own rendered PLP (method 1, displayed PLP total), captured via Playwright since the site is fully client-rendered (SAP Commerce/Spartacus-style Angular SPA, occ-backend at api-prod.freedom.com.au) and plain HTTP fetch only returns the unrendered app shell. No other seasonal/holiday categories (Halloween, Diwali, Easter, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year, etc.) exist anywhere in the site's category tree - Australia is Southern Hemisphere so Christmas naturally falls in summer here, which does not affect classification.
